title: Wishlist
summary: Buyers can save a product to buy later. This page shows how many people saved yours.

sections.title: What is a wishlist?
sections.intro: A buyer can press a heart on a product to save it and come back later. That saved list is their wishlist. A save is a sign of interest. It is not an order.

blocks.title: In simple words
items: This page shows which of your products are saved most, and the total number of saves.
You see how many people saved a product. You never see who.
You cannot change anything here. It is only for reading.
You learn which birds buyers like most.
A product that is saved often but never bought may have a price that is too high, or pictures that are not good enough. Check it.
It helps you decide what to breed or buy next.
It is free information: buyers tell you what they want without a word.

items.means: Your 50 most saved products with the total saves.
The "Wishlist demand" section: total saves, how many products were saved, and your top five.
A "Saved by" column on each product, and the sort "Most saved first".
"Saved by N customers" next to the status.

blocks.title: How to use it
steps: Look at the top of the list. These are your most wanted products.
Open a popular product. Check the price, the pictures and the stock.
If you have little stock, add more before buyers come back.

blocks.text: A product that is switched off or out of stock can still be saved. Buyers may be waiting for it to come back.
